setting: a tiny camp on the coast rocks beside a tide pool at low tide, at blue hour in the fog, seen from a crab's height: a little lean-to of three bleached driftwood sticks, with a strip of dried bull kelp laid over its ridge pole, stands on a flat rock ledge at the pool's edge, where five small friends share a thermos of cocoa by a hanging paper lantern while the tide is out; nothing else is there, no buildings, no boats, no lighthouse and no camp clutter
pet: the sea otter sits on the ledge under the lean-to, holding a mug of cocoa on its belly in both paws, watching the puffin's float; the ochre sea star sits beside the otter, leaning a little against it; the decorator crab sits on a small rock just below the lantern, warming its claws in its light; the tufted puffin stands on the near rim of the tide pool right of the lean-to with its rod on its shoulder, its float hanging in the air; farther out on the outer rocks to the right, the black oystercatcher stands small in its yellow sou'wester, looking out to sea. All five are awake and quiet
props: a small paper lantern hanging lit from the front of the lean-to's ridge pole on a short cord
a dented tin thermos of cocoa standing on the ledge beside the otter
the otter's clay mug of cocoa
the puffin's tiny fishing rod resting on its shoulder, the red-and-white float hanging in the air from the line below the rod's tip
signature: the puffin's float swinging on its line in the sea breeze, while the fog drifts past the sea stacks, the surf washes the far rocks and the lantern sways
signature_detail: A tiny hermit crab carrying its barnacled shell climbs up out of the tide pool where the ledge slopes into the water, stops at the waterline, walks across the lantern-lit ledge in front of the decorator crab's feet, stopping now and then, and goes in under the otter's raised hind foot. Added in animation, not in the painting.
stages: the paper lantern hanging from the lean-to's ridge pole
the flat top of the rock along the tide pool's near rim
open foggy sky over the sea
the flat top of a far sea stack
the still water of the tide pool
composition: the camera sits low on the rock ledge at the friends' eye level, looking across the tide pool toward the sea. The lean-to's driftwood sticks frame the upper left and roof the friends: the otter and the sea star sit under it left of center, the crab on its small rock just in front of them below the lantern. The puffin stands on the pool's near rim right of center, with the pool in front of it and beyond it. The oystercatcher is small on the outer rocks in the right third, a clear dark shape against the pale fog. Two or three sea stacks stand in the fog in the background, right of center, and quiet open fog fills the upper right. Each friend stands clear of the others and of the lean-to's sticks. Locked-off, wide 16:9
foreground: along the bottom edge, the near rim of the tide pool: a few broad, flat, dark rocks crusted with mussels and barnacles, painted simply; on the right, the near part of the tide pool, clear still water over a few green sea anemones and a strand of seaweed
midground: on a flat rock ledge left of center, under a little lean-to of three bleached driftwood sticks with a strip of dried bull kelp laid over its ridge pole and a small lit paper lantern hanging from the front of the ridge pole on a short cord: the sea otter sits holding a clay mug of cocoa on its belly in both paws, a dented tin thermos standing on the rock beside it, and the ochre sea star sits next to the otter; the decorator crab sits on a small rock just below the lantern. Right of center the tufted puffin stands on the pool's rim with its rod over its shoulder reaching out over the tide pool, the line hanging straight down from the rod's tip to the red-and-white float resting on the still water. The tide pool is wide, flat and calm, softly mirroring the fog, with a few rocks breaking its surface
background: past the pool, low-tide rocks run out toward the sea, and on the outer rocks in the right third stands the black oystercatcher, small, looking out to sea. Beyond them the sea at low tide lies gray-green and calm, with low swells and a thin line of soft white foam where it washes around the base of the far rocks. Two or three tall sea stacks with a few wind-bent spruces on top stand in the fog, the farther ones fading to pale flat shapes, and soft banks of fog lie low over the water. No moon, no stars, no sun and no sunset colors. The air near the camera is clear: no rain
light: blue hour in fog: the fog glows a soft, cool blue-gray, palest low over the sea, and the rocks, the pool and the friends' backs sit in cool slate-blue shadow. One warm light: the paper lantern hanging from the lean-to, lighting the underside of the driftwood, the fronts of the otter, the sea star and the crab, the thermos and the near edge of the pool, and fading softly and evenly into the cool dusk within about the lean-to's width, with no hard edge. The puffin catches only a little of it, a dark shape with a pale face against the pale water, and the oystercatcher is a dark silhouette against the fog. No glow halos; about half the frame is dim
